sections.heading: Where this sits for you
body: **38 of the official questions in Equivalent expressions are this one** — 21 Easy, 15 Medium, 2 Hard.
It is bottom-heavy, which makes it cheap points. Secure it early.

sections.heading: How to spot it
body: You are looking at this pattern when:
- You're given a sum, difference or product of polynomials in parentheses, sometimes after being told what one or two letters or functions stand for, and asked which choice is equivalent.
- All four choices are simplified polynomials that differ only in a sign or one coefficient.

sections.heading: The method
body: - 1) If you're given definitions (letters or f(x), g(x)), substitute them inside parentheses first.
- 2) Distribute every factor and every minus sign to every term inside its bracket.
- 3) Group terms by the same power of the variable (and the same variable) and add their coefficients.

sections.heading: Where Desmos fits
body: Type the original expression as y1 and each choice as y2.
The right choice lies exactly on top of the original.
You can also use a table and check that both give the same value at x = 2 and x = -1.

sections.heading: What it is built to catch
body: You apply a leading minus sign only to the first term inside the second bracket.
Or you add unlike terms (x² with x, or xy with x²y) as if they were the same, or add exponents when you should only add coefficients.

sections.heading: You are losing these
